evidence.summary: Canada’s Named Research Organizations list and the US Entity List both name the Institute of Applied Physics and Computational Mathematics, in Beijing, among the known aliases of the China Academy of Engineering Physics (CAEP), which the US Commerce Department describes as the technology complex responsible for the research, development and testing of China’s nuclear weapons. The institute describes itself as a multidisciplinary research institution whose main work is major national research tasks, alongside basic and applied theoretical research, and lists military science and technology progress awards among its more than 500 awards. CASI reports that the institute, founded in 1958, carries out nuclear-warhead design computations for CAEP.

CASI’s directory of China’s defence key laboratories lists the institute as host of the national defence science and technology key laboratory of computational physics, set up in 1992, whose first research direction is numerical simulation of nuclear-weapon physics.
